sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Enid, also spelled Enide, is an Arthurian heroine. She stands as the model of a loyal wife. She ranks among the Three Splendid Women of Camelot beside Dyfr and Tegau Eurfron. The knight Erec proved his worth on adventures to win her. One quest took him to hunt a white stag. After the marriage he retired from his duties to her company. Court gossip said love had made him unworthy. Enid saw that he must hear the rumor. She arranged for Erec to overhear the words. His pride stung, he rode out to redeem his name with Enid at his side. Many trials followed and both returned in honor. The Welsh retelling calls the husband Geraint.
